scope: CBSE Class 6 Mathematics · Ganita Prakash · Chapter 2 · Lines and Angles
claimBoundary: This is deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios. It is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, accessibility certification, or school-specific pacing validation.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 2 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked required assessment type, a privacy-safe learner action, and an observable mastery criterion. Geometry-tool activities must remain ordinary classroom-paper tasks and must not require camera capture, location, cloud AI, or remote monitoring.

scenarios.need: Learner classifies a drawn object by how long it looks on the page instead of using endpoint and extension properties.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: classifying by drawn length instead of defining properties
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Mark endpoints and arrow directions on a small paper sketch, then state whether each object is a segment, line or ray and justify the choice from those properties.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly classifies a new mixed set of segments, lines and rays and explains each answer using endpoints and extension rather than apparent length.

scenarios.need: Learner understands that a ray has one endpoint but reverses the ray name without noticing that the starting point changes.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: reversing ray names without changing the endpoint
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Underline the first letter in each ray name, identify it as the endpoint, and compare two labelled paper diagrams before answering.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Names three new rays correctly, identifies each endpoint, and explains why ray AB and ray BA are generally different rays.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes that a visibly longer pair of angle arms creates a larger angle even when the amount of turn is unchanged.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: longer arms make a larger angle
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Trace or redraw two angles with different arm lengths but the same opening, then compare only the amount of turn from one arm to the other.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly compares a new pair of equal-opening angles with different arm lengths and states that arm length does not determine angle size.

scenarios.need: Learner recognises a right angle only when it is drawn in a familiar upright orientation and misclassifies the same angle after rotation.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: a tilted right angle stops being right
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Rotate the paper or compare the angle against a paper-corner right-angle benchmark without photographing or uploading the work.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Identifies right angles correctly across at least four orientations and explains that rotation changes orientation, not the 90-degree turn.

scenarios.need: Learner places a protractor near the angle but does not align its centre with the vertex, producing a plausible-looking but invalid reading.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a standard classroom protractor on a printed or hand-drawn angle: align the centre mark with the vertex, place one arm on the zero baseline, then read the intersected scale.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Measures two new angles within the expected classroom tolerance while explicitly demonstrating centre, baseline and scale alignment before recording each value.

scenarios.need: Learner aligns a protractor correctly but always reads the same printed scale, including when the starting arm uses the opposite zero.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: always reading one printed protractor scale
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Circle the zero used by the starting arm before reading the scale and estimate whether the angle should be acute or obtuse as a reasonableness check.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Reads three mixed-orientation protractor diagrams from the correct zero and rejects an opposite-scale answer that conflicts with the angle classification.

scenarios.need: Learner needs a fully offline route for geometry practice and cannot depend on video, microphone, camera, cloud AI or remote teacher monitoring.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached Kiki text, locally rendered diagrams, paper and pencil, plus a paper corner if helpful; submit a selected or written response locally with no network-dependent tutoring step.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes the comparison/classification worked example and mastery check using only offline local resources and gives a correct reason for each classification.

scenarios.need: Learner can draw two roughly equal smaller angles inside a larger angle but treats visual appearance alone as proof that a bisector has been constructed.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: treating a visual midpoint as proof of an angle bisector
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Measure both resulting angles with a classroom protractor and record the two degree values; use equality of measured angle sizes as the verification rather than a photo or visual guess.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Verifies a new proposed angle bisector by measuring both parts, reports equal measures within ordinary classroom-tool tolerance, and explains why appearance alone is insufficient evidence.
